cycle_protocol.CYCLE_NEW_VIEW: Use the exact Legendre pullback lambda=4t^2/(t^2-1)^2 and the cross-factor branch pair r2 in A+B, r4 in A-B to compute the Sha/Brauer character topologically rather than reusing reducible-fiber component incidence.

exact_new_information: The fixed Jacobian is the Legendre pullback y^2=x(x+A^2)(x+B^2) with A=t^2-1, B=2t and lambda=B^2/A^2. Tr=(0,0) is twice each of two explicit rational order-4 points. Hence the previously certified I4 relative class 2 is already rational torsion primitive glue and cannot orient J2 in the marked K3 discriminant by itself. The genuinely new selector data is the horizontal f2 branch pair: r2 lies on A+B=0 and r4 on A-B=0.

f2_horizontal_character.cross_factor_property: r2 is a root of A+B while r4 is a root of A-B

lattice_reduction.new_exact_invariant: The I4/I2 relative component pattern is entirely explained by rational 4-torsion primitive glue; f2 ramifies across the two distinct lambda=1 factors A+B and A-B, so the remaining orientation data is horizontal/monodromic.

primitive_torsion_glue_reduction.I2_reason: Tr has component class 0 in Z/2, so the two bisection branches differing by Tr have the same I2 component.
primitive_torsion_glue_reduction.I4_reason: Since 2*Pplus=Tr and Tr has component class 2 in Z/4, Pplus has an odd component class and doubling the rational 4-torsion glue gives exactly the relative class 2.
primitive_torsion_glue_reduction.attempt2_relative_component_pattern: I4:(0,2) at all four I4; I2:same component at all four I2
primitive_torsion_glue_reduction.exact_remaining_information: The selector must use the horizontal f2 ramification character (or an equivalent MW/frame/topological monodromy or B-field adapter), not the relative reducible-fiber component vector by itself.

rational_4torsion_halves_of_Tr.consequence: Tr is rationally 2-divisible on the fixed Jacobian; the repaired J2 kernel direction is therefore the double of a rational order-4 torsion direction.

source_lock.torsion_primitive_closure_theorem: Schuett-Shioda, Elliptic Surfaces, arXiv:0907.0298, primitive closure of the trivial lattice / trivial lattice equals MW torsion
